verdict.summary: IREN's AI cloud transition is commercially meaningful, but the August 27 results reset the operating baseline and leave the chart without a post-event base. FY2026 revenue rose to $707.0 million from $501.0 million, with AI cloud revenue surging to $128.8 million from $16.4 million. Q4 AI cloud revenue more than doubled sequentially to $70.5 million while mining revenue fell to $66.7 million. The cost is visible: FY GAAP net loss was $702.6 million after $638.8 million of impairment, Q4 non-GAAP adjusted EBITDA was only $19.2 million, and the filing reports $5.896 billion cash, $1.724 billion restricted cash and roughly $7.593 billion debt. Management's $4 billion contracted ARR is non-GAAP and may materially exceed recognized revenue; $2.8 billion GPU financing covers 90% of associated capex but adds obligations. About $1 billion had been sold under a $6 billion ATM. The D+ grade remains a quality judgment; trade status is wait until regular-session price discovery forms a new base.

business.overview:
IREN operates bitcoin mining sites and is redeploying power, datacenter shells and capital toward GPU cloud services. Revenue is driven by hash production and bitcoin economics in mining, and by commissioned accelerators, utilization and contract delivery in AI cloud.

The AI transmission channel is direct: secured power supports GPU clusters, customer contracts and financing fund accelerator purchases, and cloud revenue begins as installed systems enter service. Q4 AI cloud revenue of $70.5M versus $66.7M of mining revenue shows the transition reaching operating scale.

The model breaks if contracted ARR fails to convert into recognized revenue, GPU economics compress, financing obligations outrun deployment, or mining cash flow deteriorates during the transition. The $638.8M annual impairment proves specialized hardware can lose value quickly. Investors must distinguish $5.896B of cash from $1.724B of restricted cash and compare both with roughly $7.593B of debt before assigning value to future cloud capacity.
business.moat: IREN controls renewable-powered campuses and has demonstrated rapid GPU-cloud deployment while retaining mining cash generation. The moat is speed and power access, not the accounting ARR label; hardware refresh cycles and customer concentration can erase the advantage.

earnings.beatNote: FY2026 revenue was $707.0M versus $501.0M, including AI cloud revenue of $128.8M versus $16.4M and bitcoin-mining revenue of $578.2M versus $484.6M. FY GAAP net loss was $702.6M after $638.8M of impairment; non-GAAP adjusted EBITDA was $245.7M versus $269.7M. Q4 revenue was $137.2M, AI cloud revenue $70.5M, mining revenue $66.7M, GAAP net loss $684.0M and adjusted EBITDA $19.2M. Management cited $4B of contracted ARR and $1B of operating ARR in August but did not issue formal FY2027 consolidated revenue guidance; contracted ARR is non-GAAP and may materially exceed recognized revenue. The key caveat is whether commissioned capacity converts those contracts into revenue and cash before financing and hardware depreciation consume the economics. No confirmed IREN next-earnings date was announced with the August annual results or official calendar checked.

capitalStructure.shareHistory: IREN reports exactly 380,710,559 ordinary shares outstanding at June 30, including 47,165,838 shares sold under the March $6B ATM for $2.492B gross and the completed 39,699,102-share registered direct offering. Six convert series were outstanding: the remaining 2029/2030 notes plus $1.0B 2031, $1.15B 2032, $1.15B June-2033 and the May 14 $3.0B 1.00% December-2033 notes; initial prices imply roughly 127.2M gross conversion shares if all settled entirely in stock. Subsequent claims include 18,198,656 co-CEO RSUs and up to 30M NVIDIA investment rights. A fixed fully diluted count is unavailable because note settlement can be cash, shares or both, rates can adjust, and awards vest over time. The minimum observable legal denominator remains 380.7M; quantified claims are disclosed separately rather than netted against capped calls.

filings.finding: The March Form 10-Q provides the pre-year-end operating and balance-sheet baseline; the later August 2026 Form 10-K controls annual revenue, cash, impairment and debt conclusions.
The FY2026 Form 10-K reports $707.0M revenue, $638.8M impairment, $5.896B cash, $1.724B restricted cash and approximately $7.593B debt. These filed annual values control the editorial conclusion.

The August earnings Form 8-K furnishes FY2026 results and the AI-cloud operating update; it supports $4B contracted ARR while identifying that measure as non-GAAP. This classification controls the editorial conclusion.

The July 1 Form 8-K reports Board approval of 9,099,328 RSUs for each co-CEO, or 18,198,656 awards in aggregate, subject to a combined six-year vesting and holding period; these are quantified dilution claims, not shares already issued.

The May 14 Form 8-K records completion of $3.0B of 1.00% convertible senior notes due December 2033, including the fully exercised $400M option, at 13.6848 shares per $1,000 or approximately 41.05M gross conversion shares before adjustments; it is debt with potential equity settlement, not common issuance.

The March 424B5 establishes a $6B at-the-market common-share program; about $1B sold is completed issuance, while the unsold authorization remains capacity rather than proceeds. This classification controls the editorial conclusion.

The definitive December 424B5 sold 39,699,102 ordinary shares at $41.12 for $1.632B in a registered direct primary offering. It also describes concurrent $1.0B 0.25% 2032 notes and $1.0B 1.00% 2033 notes, each with a $150M option; debt and equity must remain separate.

The preliminary December 424B5 proposed the same registered direct ordinary-share sale and concurrent 2032/2033 convertible-note program later finalized in accession 0001140361-25-044381. It is a program stage, not a second completed issuance, and must not be double-counted.

This EFFECT notice confirms only that IREN's referenced registration statement became effective; it establishes no security amount, completed ATM sale, debt issuance, warrant exercise or financing proceeds by itself.
